**Write time.** 

More precisely: **once per phase close**, when appending into the prefix. Any token selection that happens *ahead* of the stable prefix rewrites existing bytes, which is exactly what triggers the volatile-bit law (FM-2, FM-3, header seqRange, FM-7) and voids the cache. But appending at the very back—during summarization, deciding which raw lines/tokens survive into a branch’s summary or the FM-6 Zone C window—touches no cached bytes at all. It costs a single deliberate 1.25× cache epoch and pays forward 0.1× re-read savings for every subsequent turn. That’s why the team concluded the legitimate home for DSA-on-tokens isn’t the per-turn prompt layer, but the summarizer itself.

Anything attempted between epochs — even at low frequency — would still rewrite within the cached span and trigger re-bills, which is exactly why per-turn token DSA kept failing across loops 2–6.
